To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 9-deoxomacrolides (azalides) are a novel class of macrolides with improved in vitro and in vitro activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, respectively, and that the N-methyl, 4'-epimers of erythromycins A and B are the most active compounds in the azalide series.

(1) the 9-deoxonine ring-expanded macrocyclic lactones are a new class of semisynthetic macrolides; (2) these azalides exhibit improved in vitro and in vitro antibacterial activity, including Gram-negative potency, when compared to erythryomycin A; (3) the 4''-epimeric and 4''-amine substituted azalides are the most interesting compounds; (4) these compounds have advanced to clinical evaluation.

the new azalides, in general, exhibit improved Gram-negative activity and pharmacokinetic properties.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the basic nitrogen atom in the macrocyclic lactam ring is a critical determinant of azalide activity, and that the C-4' hydroxyl group is a key determinant of azalide stability in vivo.
